learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of the engineering disciplines specific to their specialization, at the necessary level to acquire the rest of the degree's competencies, including notions of the latest advances.
Awareness of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.

The ability to analyze complex products, processes, and systems in their field of study; to choose and appropriately apply established analytical, calculation, and experimental methods and to correctly interpret the results of such analyses.

The ability to identify, formulate, and solve engineering problems in their specialization; to choose and appropriately apply established analytical, calculation, and experimental methods; to recognize the importance of social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial constraints.

Ability to project, design, and develop complex products (parts, components, finished products, etc.), processes, and systems in their specialization, that meet established requirements, including awareness of social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial aspects; as well as to select and apply appropriate project methods.
Project ability using some cutting-edge knowledge of their engineering specialization.

Ability to perform bibliographic searches, consult and critically use databases and other information sources, to carry out simulation and analysis with the aim of conducting research on technical topics in their specialization.
Ability to consult and apply good practice and safety codes in their specialization.
Ability and skill to design and carry out experimental research, interpret results, and reach conclusions in their field of study.
Understanding of applicable techniques and methods of analysis, project, and research, and their limitations in the scope of their specialization.
Practical competence to solve complex problems, carry out complex engineering projects, and conduct research specific to their specialization.
Knowledge of the application of materials, equipment and tools, technology and engineering processes, and their limitations in the scope of their specialization.
Ability to apply engineering practice standards in their specialization.
Knowledge of the social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial implications of engineering practice.
General ideas on economic, organizational, and management issues (such as project management, risk management, and change management) in the industrial and business context.
Ability to collect and interpret data and manage complex concepts within their specialization, to make judgments that involve reflection on ethical and social issues.
Ability to manage complex technical or professional activities or projects in their specialization, taking responsibility for decision-making.
Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions in the field of engineering and with society in general.
Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in a team, and to cooperate with both engineers and people from other disciplines.
Ability to recognize the need for continuous self-training and to undertake this activity throughout their professional life independently.
Ability to stay updated on science and technology developments.

syllabus_topics: Presentation and defense of the work

assessment_methods.method: Presentation and defense before a university tribunal
